Answer: C
Reason: The axial CT image demonstrates a well-circumscribed anterior mediastinal mass with a distinct, thick calcified rim and heterogeneous internal contents (including fat density), which are classic radiological features of a mature teratoma. While the patient has a history of breast cancer, the specific morphology of this lesion (calcified wall and mixed composition) strongly points to a benign teratoma rather than a metastasis or other mediastinal tumors.
